s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to assemble together, with the possible implication of compactness or solidarity
s.g: to gather together; to come together

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to cause to gather together (compare συναθροίζομαι, {D:15.130})
s.g: to cause to come together; to gather together; to call together

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to assemble together, with emphasis on the element of togetherness (compare {L:ἀθροίζω<SDBG:ἀθροίζω:000000>}, {D:15.129})
s.g: to gather together

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to live in association with or together with someone else
s.g: to live together with; to live with
s.c: In ⟦2 Corinthians 7:3|2 Corinthians 7:3⟧ it is important to note that συζάω should not be understood in the sense of inhabiting the same house with someone else. The reference here is the sense of unity and comradeship rather than dwelling in the same place.

s.d: to join two persons in a marriage relationship
s.g: to cause to be married; to join in marriage

s.d: to express forceful differences of opinion without necessarily having a presumed goal of seeking a solution
s.g: to dispute; dispute

s.d: to converse with someone, including a clear implication as to reciprocal response
s.g: to talk with; to speak with; to converse

s.d: (derivative of {L:συζητέω<SDBG:συζητέω:000000>}[a] ‘to debate, to dispute,’ {D:33.440}) a person who is skilled in or likely to be involved in expressing strong differences of opinion
s.g: debater; disputer

s.d: one who is closely linked with another in some activity{N:001}
s.g: fellow worker
s.c: Some scholars, however, interpret σύζυγος in ⟦Philippians 4:3|Philippians 4:3⟧ as being a proper name.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to cause to live again together with others
s.g: to raise to life together with
s.c: There are serious semantic difficulties involved in a literal translation of συνεγείρω or συζωοποιέω, for a literal rendering could either be interpreted as ‘to be raised to life at the same time with’ or ‘to be raised to life in the same way as,’ but the reference in ⟦Colossians 3:1|Colossians 3:1⟧ and ⟦Ephesians 2:5|Ephesians 2:5⟧ is to a spiritual existence more than to a literal resurrection of the body. This means that both συνεγείρω and συζωοποιέω must be understood as highly figurative. Hence, in ⟦Colossians 3:1|Colossians 3:1⟧ it may be necessary to translate εἰ οὖν συνηγέρθητε τῷ Χριστῷ as ‘since you have been raised to life, so to speak, with Christ’ or ‘since, as it were, you have been raised to life with Christ.’ In this way one may point to the fact of a figurative element involved.

s.d: a deciduous fruit tree growing to about 6 m; produces black berries containing a sweet reddish juice
s.g: mulberry tree
s.c: For languages which have no specific term for ‘mulberry tree,’ one can often employ a generic expression followed by a type of classifier, for example, ‘the tree called mulberry’ (in which case the term ‘mulberry’ may be borrowed from a dominant language of the area) or ‘a tree producing berries’; but in ⟦Luke 17:6|Luke 17:6⟧ the focus is upon the tree as a large object and not upon the type of fruit which it produced. One can, therefore, say simply ‘this tree.’

s.d: fruit tree; grows 5-8 m high; round crown and very deep roots; Ficus carica; fruit is about the size of a hen’s egg and can be green, yellow, purple, or brown depending on the type, and is sweet and soft
s.g: fig tree
s.c: In Palestine the fig tree occurs in both wild and cultivated forms and the latter is greatly valued for its sweet, edible fruit. It normally produces two crops each year: early figs ripening in June (late spring) and late ones in August and September (early fall).|For languages in which a term for ‘fig tree’ is not known, one can often employ a borrowed term with a so-called ‘classifier,’ for example, ‘a tree called fig’ or ‘a fruit tree producing fruit called figs.’ In many tropical areas of the world there are forest trees belonging to the botanical family of fig trees, but such trees generally produce inedible fruit. It may, however, be possible for a translator to use the term for such a forest tree but with the added explanation as to the fruit- bearing quality of the trees mentioned in the Bible.

s.d: a broad, heavy tree reaching a height of some fifteen meters (about fifty feet), with large, strong branches growing out from the trunk low down on the tree; fruit has the appearance of a small fig but its taste is relatively unpleasant
s.g: sycamore-fig tree
s.c: As in the case of other specific trees for which no local term in the receptor language is available, one can borrow a word such as ‘sycamore’ from a dominant language in the area and add a classifier, for example, ‘tree called sycamore,’ but in a number of languages it may be appropriate to render συκομορέα in ⟦Luke 19:4|Luke 19:4⟧ simply as ‘a big tree’ or ‘a wild fig tree.’

s.d: the fruit of the fig tree
s.g: fig
s.c: As in the case of the corresponding term for the fig tree (LN 3.5), it may be best to borrow a term for fig and add a classifier, for example, ‘fruit called fig.’

s.d: to bring false charges against someone, especially with the intent of personal profit
s.g: to make false charges
s.c: The term συκοφαντέω refers to a practice in which persons could bring charges against an individual and receive a part of the fine or indemnity paid to the court.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of συλαγωγέω ‘to carry off as booty or as captive in war,’ not occurring in the NT) to take over complete control of a person as one would a captive
s.g: to control completely; to take control of; to make a captive of
s.c: In some languages it is possible to preserve the figurative meaning of συλαγωγέω in ⟦Colossians 2:8|Colossians 2:8⟧ by employing a simile, for example, ‘see that no one makes you a kind of captive by human wisdom’ or ‘see to it that no one uses human wisdom and by this means makes you, so to speak, a captive.’

s.d: to take by force that which belongs to someone else (often used of taking spoils of war, but occurring in the NT only figuratively of Pauls accepting financial support from some churches in order to help others)
s.g: to rob

s.d: to converse with someone, including a clear implication as to reciprocal response
s.g: to talk with; to speak with; to converse

s.dp: Control, Rule › Seize, Take into Custody
s.d: to seize and to take along with
s.g: to seize; to catch; to take; to arrest

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Birth, Procreation
s.g: to conceive; to become pregnant
s.c: In many languages the process of becoming pregnant is expressed in different ways: ‘to begin to become large,’ ‘to receive sperm,’ ‘to let a child enter,’ or ‘to stop bleeding’ (a reference to the cessation of menstrual periods).|The phrases ἐν γαστρί (⟦Luke 1:31|Luke 1:31⟧) and ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ (⟦Luke 2:21|Luke 2:21⟧), meaning ‘in the womb,’ may be added to συλλαμβάνω without significant alteration of its meaning.

s.d: to help by joining in an activity or effort
s.g: to join in helping
s.c: In a number of instances it is not necessary to specify the joint effort or activity, since this is supplied by the context itself as, for example, in ⟦Luke 5:7|Luke 5:7⟧ in which ‘coming to help’ indicates clearly the joint efforts. But in some languages it may be important to use a specific expression rather than a generic one. Accordingly, ‘to come and help them’ in ⟦Luke 5:7|Luke 5:7⟧ may be rendered as ‘to come and work with them.’

s.d: to pluck or pick by pulling off or out of, with the intent of gathering together
s.g: to pick; to pluck
s.c: See footnote at τρυγάω LN 43.18.

s.d: to converse with someone, including a clear implication as to reciprocal response
s.g: to talk with; to speak with; to converse

s.d: to feel sorrow or grief together with someone or at the same time
s.g: to feel sorry for

s.d: to happen, with the implication of occurring in connection with other events
s.g: to happen

s.d: to give careful consideration to various implications of an issue
s.g: to reflect on; to think about seriously; to think deeply about

s.d: to confer, implying a series of proposals
s.g: to confer
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to confer’ is ‘to discuss what should be done’ or ‘to talk about plans.’

s.d: to express differences of opinion in a forceful way, involving alternative opportunities for presenting contrasting viewpoints
s.g: to debate; to discuss forcefully

s.d: to meet and join up with, with either friendly or hostile intent
s.g: to join up with; to meet
s.c: In instances in which meeting up with someone may be either friendly or hostile, it is frequently necessary to select terms which will indicate clearly the relation or intention of the participants. In most languages a purely neutral term of ‘meeting’ would be misleading.

s.d: to assist in supplying what may be needed{N:001}
s.g: to help

s.d: to reign as a king together with someone else{N:001}
s.g: to be kings together; to reign with
s.c: Used figuratively in ⟦1 Corinthians 4:8|1 Corinthians 4:8⟧.

s.d: to bring together into a unit
s.g: to bring together; to cause to be a unit; to unite; to combine

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:συμβιβάζω<SDBG:συμβιβάζω:000000>}[a] ‘to bring together, to unite, to combine,’ {D:63.5}) to come to a solution or a decision, implying a process of putting together different aspects of related information
s.g: to conclude; to decide; to infer

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be known as certain and therefore dependable
s.g: to show for certain; to prove
s.c: In a number of languages one may express certainty by a negative phrase, for example, ‘so that no one could ever doubt.’ In other instances, an idiomatic expression may be used, for example, ‘with heavy words’ or ‘with words that speak to the heart’ or ‘with words that are like rocks.’

s.d: to advise by giving instructions
s.g: to advise; to instruct

s.d: to tell someone what he or she should plan to do
s.g: to advise; to counsel

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: to engage in joint planning so as to devise a course of common action, often one with a harmful or evil purpose
s.g: to confer; to consult; to plot; to make plans against

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: to engage in joint planning so as to devise a course of common action, often one with a harmful or evil purpose
s.g: to confer; to consult; to plot; to make plans against

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: an advisory council
s.g: council
s.c: In ⟦Acts 25:12|Acts 25:12⟧ it is possible to render ‘council’ as ‘those persons who gave him their opinions’ or ‘those who were his advisors’ or even ‘those who said what should be done’ or ‘… what was best to do.’

s.d: (derivative of {L:συμβουλεύω<SDBG:συμβουλεύω:000000>} ‘to advise,’ {D:33.294}) one who gives advice
s.g: adviser

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: one form of the apostle Peter’s Aramaic name
s.g: Simeon

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a son of Jacob and ancestor of an Israelite tribe
s.g: Simeon

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: an elderly man of Jerusalem ({S:04200202500018})
s.g: Simeon

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian prophet at Antioch who was also called Niger
s.g: Simeon

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus
s.g: Simeon

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: a person who along with someone else is a disciple or follower
s.g: fellow disciple
s.c: The phrase ‘his fellow disciples’ may be expressed in some languages as ‘disciples along with him’ or ‘those who were disciples even as he was.’

s.d: to provide confirming evidence by means of a testimony
s.g: to support by testimony; to provide supporting evidence; to testify in support
s.c: It may be necessary in some languages to translate this phrase in ⟦Romans 2:15|Romans 2:15⟧ as ‘their consciences say to them that this is true.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: to share in something by having an appropriate part
s.g: to share in; to have a part of together with others

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: (derivative of συμμετέχω ‘to share in the possession of something,’ not occurring in the NT) one who shares in a possession or a relationship
s.g: sharer; partner

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Imitate Behavior
s.d: one who joins others as an imitator
s.g: to join as an imitator; to be an imitator together with others; joint imitator

s.d: to come to be similar in form to something else
s.g: to share in having the likeness of; to take on the same form as; to become like
s.c: In some languages a more appropriate equivalent of this expression in ⟦Philippians 3:10|Philippians 3:10⟧ may be ‘to come to be like him in his death’ or ‘to die in a manner similar to his death.’

s.d: pertaining to that which has a similar form or nature
s.g: similar in form; of the same form
s.c: In the case of ⟦Romans 8:29|Romans 8:29⟧ it may be necessary in some languages to translate ‘he set them apart in order that they might be like his Son,’ and in ⟦Philippians 3:21|Philippians 3:21⟧ it may be necessary in some languages to translate ‘having a glorious body like his.’

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: to suffer along with someone else
s.g: to suffer with; to share in the sufferings of
s.c: It is, however, possible to interpret συμπαθέω in ⟦Hebrews 10:34|Hebrews 10:34⟧ as referring primarily to sympathy rather than actual sharing or suffering.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: to share someone’s feeling in the sense of being sympathetic with
s.g: to be sympathetic toward; to have sympathy for
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of ‘being sympathetic with’ may be ‘to understand completely how one feels’ or ‘to feel in one’s heart just like someone else feels.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to feeling sympathy for someone or something
s.g: sympathetic

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: the movement of two or more objects to the same location{N:001}
s.g: to gather together; to come together; to go together; to meet; to assemble
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

s.d: to be encouraged at the same time with someone else
s.g: to be encouraged together; to be encouraged at the same time

s.d: to take along with, with emphasis upon accompaniment
s.g: to take along; to bring along with

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be in a place together with others
s.g: to be with; to be present with

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: to undergo the same type of suffering as others do
s.g: to join in suffering; to assume one’s share of suffering; to suffer together

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send someone together with someone else
s.g: to send with; to send together
s.c: In some languages it may be difficult to express in a succinct way the meaning of ‘to send with.’ For example, in ⟦2 Corinthians 8:22|2 Corinthians 8:22⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘they are going and so we are causing our Christian brother to go with them,’ and in ⟦2 Corinthians 12:18|2 Corinthians 12:18⟧ one may translate ‘I begged Titus to go, and I caused the other Christian brother to go with him.’

s.d: to embrace, as an expression of great concern for someone
s.g: to embrace; to hug
s.c: In the translation of συμπεριλαμβάνω in ⟦Acts 20:10|Acts 20:10⟧ it is essential to avoid any implication of erotic motivations.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: drink together with others
s.g: to drink together
s.c: In rendering ⟦Acts 10:41|Acts 10:41⟧ it may be necessary to restructure somewhat the expression of joint activity, for example, ‘we and he drank together’ or ‘he was one with us in drinking together.’ In some languages it may seem strange to speak of ‘eating and drinking,’ since both of these activities are often subsumed under a term for ‘dining.’ It may therefore be preferable in some languages to translate ‘we dined together with him’ or ‘we had our meals together with him.’

s.d: (a technical, nautical term) to be swamped with water while sailing in a boat
s.g: to be swamped; to have a boat filling rapidly with water

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
s.d: to come to the end of a period of time, with the implication of the completion of an implied purpose or plan{N:001}
s.g: to complete; to come to an end
s.c: In a number of languages it may be difficult to speak of a period of time being ‘complete.’ In ⟦Luke 1:23|Luke 1:23⟧ one may often translate as ‘when he had finished his period of service’ or even ‘when he had done his work.’ In the case of ⟦Acts 7:30|Acts 7:30⟧, the expression ‘after forty years were completed’ may be rendered in some languages as ‘after forty years were passed’ or ‘when forty years had happened.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning employing the base {L:πνίγω<SDBG:πνίγω:000000>}[a] ‘to choke,’ {D:19.53}) to cause the death of plants by other plants crowding them out and/or overshadowing them{N:001}
s.g: to cause plants to die

s.d: to crowd around to the point that one can hardly breathe (a very emphatic form)
s.g: to crowd around; to press against

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Cause Trouble, Hardship
s.d: to cause serious trouble to, with the implication of dire consequences and probably a weakened state
s.g: to cause severe hardship; to oppress; to overwhelm

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a fellow member of a socio-political unit
s.g: fellow citizen
s.c: The expression in ⟦Ephesians 2:19|Ephesians 2:19⟧ may also be rendered as ‘you join with God’s people as fellow citizens together with them’ or ‘you and God’s people are all persons who belong to the same place’ or as in some languages, ‘… people of God’s country.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: to come/go together with one or more other persons
s.g: to come with; to go with; to accompany

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: the movement of two or more objects to the same location{N:001}
s.g: to gather together; to come together; to go together; to meet; to assemble
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › General
s.d: a group of persons engaged in eating together
s.g: a group eating together
s.c: Note that Luke employs κλισίας in essentially the same type of context in which Mark uses συμπόσια.

s.d: one who is an elder along with others
s.g: fellow elder

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to cause to come together, whether of animate or inanimate objects
s.g: to gather together; to call together

s.d: to be of an advantage to someone
s.g: to be advantageous; to be better off; to be to someone’s advantage
s.c: In a number of languages the idea of ‘advantage’ implies some comparison, either a benefit which is greater than someone else has or a benefit which makes one’s later state better off than the previous state. For example, in the case of ⟦John 11:50|John 11:50⟧ one may translate ‘don’t you realize that if one man dies for the people, then you are much better off.’

s.d: that which constitutes an advantage
s.g: advantage; benefit

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: to give assent to a particular proposition
s.g: to agree with; to assent to
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to give assent to’ is simply ‘to say Yes to.’ In other instances it may be important to introduce direct discourse, for example, ‘to say, I agree.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a person who is a member of the same {L:πατριά<SDBG:πατριά:000001>}[b] or {L:φυλή<SDBG:φυλή:000001>}[b] ‘nation’ ({D:11.56})
s.g: fellow countryman
s.c: The term ἄνδρες is often added to ἀδελφοί, constituting a lexical unit having essentially the same meaning as ἀδελφοί, but with the connotation of greater formality: ἄνδρες ἀδελφοίἐξὸν εἰπεῖν μετὰ παρρησίας πρὸς ὑμᾶς ‘fellow countrymen, I can speak to you quite plainly’ ⟦Acts 2:29|Acts 2:29⟧.|συμφυλέτης, συγγενής, and ἀδελφός may often be translated by a phrase, for example, ‘a person of the same country’ or ‘a man who belongs to the same nation’ or ‘one who is part of the same tribe.’

s.d: pertaining to being closely associated in a similar experience
s.g: to be like; to be one with

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to grow together with, in reference to plants
s.g: to grow together with
s.c: In rendering συναυξάνομαι (LN 23.192) and συμφύομαι, it is important to avoid an expression which will imply that two plants grew together to become a single plant. The meaning is that two or more plants grew in the same general area and at approximately the same time.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: to come to an agreement with, often implying a type of joint decision
s.g: to agree with; agreement

s.d: to be sufficiently like something as to fit or match
s.g: to be like; to match

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: coming to an agreement with, often implying a type of joint decision
s.g: agreement

s.d: melodic and rhythmic sound, produced either by several instruments or by a single instrument
s.g: music
s.c: In view of the combination of music and dancing, it will be necessary in some languages to choose a term for music which will fit this type of context, that is to say, music which would be normally employed for a dance.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: coming to an agreement with, often implying a type of joint decision
s.g: agreement

s.d: to count up or calculate a total
s.g: to count; to calculate; to add up; to figure out

s.d: pertaining to similarity of attitude and spirit
s.g: harmonious; united in spirit; being one in spirit

s.d: a marker of an associative relation, often involving joint participation in some activity{N:001}
s.g: with; together with

s.d: a marker of linkage between objects or between events, but without specifying the precise positional or functional relation
s.g: with; on; together with; at

s.dp: Case › Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
s.d: (followed by the genitive; an idiom, literally: with the hand of) a marker of an associated agent
s.g: by; with the help of

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to cause to come together, whether of animate or inanimate objects
s.g: to gather together; to call together

s.d: to collect and put in a safe place
s.g: to store; to keep in a place

s.d: to convert property or goods into money
s.g: to convert into money; to turn into money

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: the movement of two or more objects to the same location{N:002}
s.g: to gather together; to come together; to go together; to meet; to assemble
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: an assembled group of worshipers or members of such a group
s.g: assembly; congregation
s.c: In ⟦James 2:2|James 2:2⟧ συναγωγή may indicate the place of gathering, rather than the assembled group (see συναγωγή, LN 7.20).|In translating ⟦James 2:2|James 2:2⟧ it is possible to render the conditional clause as ‘if a person comes into your church’ or ‘… into your congregation.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a congregation of Jews
s.g: synagogue; congregation
s.c: Since the borrowed term ‘synagogue’ in receptor languages so frequently refers only to a building rather than to a congregation, it may be necessary in ⟦Acts 9:2|Acts 9:2⟧ to say ‘he asked for letters of introduction to leaders of the synagogues’ or ‘… leaders of the congregations of Jews.’

s.d: a building of assembly, associated with religious activity (normally a building in which Jewish worship took place and in which the Law was taught, but in {S:05900200200010} a Christian assembly place)
s.g: synagogue or Christian assembly place
s.c: It is also possible to interpret συναγωγή in ⟦James 2:2|James 2:2⟧ as a reference to an assembly of believers rather than to a building (see LN 11.44).|It is important to distinguish clearly between συναγωγή and ναός (LN 7.15) or ἱερός (LN 7.16). There were many synagogues, but only one Temple in Jerusalem, and it is not enough to speak of synagogues merely as ‘small temples.’ It is better either to borrow a term for synagogue or employ a descriptive equivalent such as ‘places where Jewish people worshiped God’ or ‘buildings for worshiping God.’|It is also important to distinguish in translating between a term for ‘synagogue’ and for ‘church,’ whether as a reference to the congregation or to the building.

s.d: to join with someone else in some severe effort
s.g: to join fervently in; to join vigorously in

s.d: to toil together with someone in a struggle, implying opposition and/or competition
s.g: to labor alongside of; to toil with

s.d: to settle or check on accounts with someone
s.g: to check on accounts; to settle accounts

s.d: one who has been arrested and imprisoned along with someone else
s.g: fellow prisoner
s.c: A strictly literal rendering of συναιχμάλωτος in the sense of ‘fellow captive’ could be misleading, since it might imply that Paul himself had been a soldier or civilian captured in a war.

s.d: to accompany someone, with explicit marking of association
s.g: to accompany; to follow

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: eating together, with emphasis upon fellowship during the process
s.g: to eat with
s.c: συναλίζομαι in ⟦Acts 1:4|Acts 1:4⟧ is interpreted by some as being συναλίζομαι to stay with (LN 41.37) on the assumption that the occurrence in ⟦Acts 1:4|Acts 1:4⟧ is simply an alternative spelling for συναυλίζομαι to stay with. This latter reading is supported by some manuscripts.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Particular Patterns of Behavior
s.d: to live in fellowship with others (a meaning of συναλίζομαι in view of its being regarded as a variant of συναυλίζομαι ‘to be with, to stay with,’ not occurring in the NT)
s.g: to live with; to be in fellowship with
s.c: συναλίζομαι in the sense of ‘to be together in fellowship’ fits well in the context of ⟦Acts 1:4|Acts 1:4⟧, but this meaning would seem to be somewhat alien to general Greek usage, and therefore συναλίζομαι is more frequently understood in the context of ⟦Acts 1:4|Acts 1:4⟧ as meaning ‘to be eating with’ (see LN 23.13).

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: to accompany in going up to
s.g: to go or come up together with; to travel with; to accompany

s.d: to be associated with others in eating
s.g: to eat together; to associate in a meal

s.d: to associate with one another, normally involving spacial proximity and/or joint activity, and usually implying some kind of reciprocal relation or involvement
s.g: to associate; to be in the company of; to be involved with; association
s.c: In translating terms referring to association, one may employ a number of different kinds of expressions, for example, ‘to have something to do with,’ ‘to keep company with,’ ‘to go around with,’ ‘to join in doing things together,’ or ‘to become a companion of.’ Sometimes association is spoken of in terms of the impression made upon others, for example, ‘to be seen often together,’ ‘to be regarded as close friends,’ and even idiomatically as ‘to be another person’s shadow.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Tire, Rest
s.d: to experience restorative rest together with someone else (see {L:ἀναπαύομαι<SDBG:ἀναπαύω:000000>}[a] ‘to rest,’ {D:23.80})
s.g: to rest together with someone else; to rest with

s.d: to happen, with the implication of that which one meets up with
s.g: to come upon; to happen to

s.d: to help by joining in an activity or effort
s.g: to join in helping
s.c: In a number of instances it is not necessary to specify the joint effort or activity, since this is supplied by the context itself as, for example, in ⟦Luke 5:7|Luke 5:7⟧ in which ‘coming to help’ indicates clearly the joint efforts. But in some languages it may be important to use a specific expression rather than a generic one. Accordingly, ‘to come and help them’ in ⟦Luke 5:7|Luke 5:7⟧ may be rendered as ‘to come and work with them.’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to cause someone else in addition to change from belief in what is true to belief in what is false
s.g: to cause to go astray together; to deceive in addition; to lead astray with

s.d: to associate with one another, normally involving spacial proximity and/or joint activity, and usually implying some kind of reciprocal relation or involvement
s.g: to associate; to be in the company of; to be involved with; association
s.c: In translating terms referring to association, one may employ a number of different kinds of expressions, for example, ‘to have something to do with,’ ‘to keep company with,’ ‘to go around with,’ ‘to join in doing things together,’ or ‘to become a companion of.’ Sometimes association is spoken of in terms of the impression made upon others, for example, ‘to be seen often together,’ ‘to be regarded as close friends,’ and even idiomatically as ‘to be another person’s shadow.’|It is also possible to interpret the phrase τοῖς ταπεινοῖς συναπαγόμενοι in ⟦Romans 12:16|Romans 12:16⟧ as meaning ‘share in doing what is humble’ (see LN 41.22).

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: to share in engaging continuously in some activity
s.g: to share; to share in doing
s.c: συναπάγομαι in ⟦Romans 12:16|Romans 12:16⟧ may also be understood as meaning ‘to involve oneself with,’ and hence one may translate ‘do not be proud, but become involved with humble people’ or ‘… make friends with humble people.’ For this interpretation, see LN 34.1.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to experience death along with others
s.g: to die together with

s.d: to be destroyed together with someone or something else
s.g: to be destroyed with; to perish with
s.c: In a number of languages one must translate συναπόλλυμαι in ⟦Hebrews 11:31|Hebrews 11:31⟧ as ‘to die,’ for example, ‘Rahab the harlot did not die with those who were disobedient.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send someone together with someone else
s.g: to send with; to send together
s.c: In some languages it may be difficult to express in a succinct way the meaning of ‘to send with.’ For example, in ⟦2 Corinthians 8:22|2 Corinthians 8:22⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘they are going and so we are causing our Christian brother to go with them,’ and in ⟦2 Corinthians 12:18|2 Corinthians 12:18⟧ one may translate ‘I begged Titus to go, and I caused the other Christian brother to go with him.’

s.dp: Arrange, Organize › Put Together, Arrange [of physical objects]
s.d: to fit together in a coherent and compatible manner{N:001}
s.g: to fit together; to be joined together

s.d: to seize or snatch by force and to take away with
s.g: to seize; to take off with
s.c: In a number of languages, one must distinguish carefully between seizure by an animate being and seizure by a force such as the wind.

s.d: to cause something to be moved off course
s.g: to force off course; to cause to go off course

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to become larger together with, in the sense of growing in essentially the same area and at the same time (compare συμφύομαι, {D:23.193})
s.g: to grow with; to grow together

s.d: that which ties something together
s.g: bindings; bonds; that which ties together
s.c: The context of ⟦Colossians 2:19|Colossians 2:19⟧ is, however, highly figurative.

s.d: that which combines or brings objects and/or events together
s.g: to bring together; to bind together; to unite

s.d: to be in prison along with others
s.g: to be in prison with; imprisonment with

s.dp: Status › Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
s.d: to receive great honor together with someone else
s.g: to be honored together with; to be exalted together with

s.d: one who is a fellow slave or a slave alongside another slave
s.g: fellow slave
s.c: In some languages there is a very strong negative connotation in any word meaning ‘slave,’ for it may suggest ‘vile person’ or even ‘foreigner,’ since in a number of areas only foreigners were made slaves. It may therefore be necessary to use a term for slave which is more or less equivalent to ‘servant,’ ‘one who works without pay,’ ‘one who must work without pay,’ or ‘bondservant.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to come together quickly to form a crowd
s.g: to rush together; to run together; to assemble quickly

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to cause to live again together with others
s.g: to raise to life together with
s.c: There are serious semantic difficulties involved in a literal translation of συνεγείρω or συζωοποιέω, for a literal rendering could either be interpreted as ‘to be raised to life at the same time with’ or ‘to be raised to life in the same way as,’ but the reference in ⟦Colossians 3:1|Colossians 3:1⟧ and ⟦Ephesians 2:5|Ephesians 2:5⟧ is to a spiritual existence more than to a literal resurrection of the body. This means that both συνεγείρω and συζωοποιέω must be understood as highly figurative. Hence, in ⟦Colossians 3:1|Colossians 3:1⟧ it may be necessary to translate εἰ οὖν συνηγέρθητε τῷ Χριστῷ as ‘since you have been raised to life, so to speak, with Christ’ or ‘since, as it were, you have been raised to life with Christ.’ In this way one may point to the fact of a figurative element involved.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a socio-political group acting as a judicial council
s.g: city council; council of judges
s.c: There are certain problems involved in the rendering of συνέδριον as ‘city council,’ since in so many parts of the world a group which would be designated as a ‘city council’ would be primarily legislative rather than judicial in function. It is for that reason that συνέδριον may be better translated in a number of instances as ‘the council which will judge you‘ or ‘before a group of men who will decide whether you have done right or wrong.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: the highest Jewish council, exercising jurisdiction in civil and religious matters, but having no power over life and death or over military actions or taxation{N:001}
s.g: Sanhedrin; the council of the Jews
s.c: In a number of languages συνέδριον can be rendered by a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘the most important council of the Jews’ or ‘the council that made decisions for the Jewish people.’

s.d: to be aware of information about something
s.g: to know; to be conscious of; to be aware of

s.d: (contrast {L:συνείδησις<SDBG:συνείδησις:000000>}[a] ‘knowledge about something,’ {D:28.4}) the psychological faculty which can distinguish between right and wrong
s.g: moral sensitivity; conscience
s.c: In some languages συνείδησις may be rendered as ‘the inner voice’ or ‘the voice in one’s heart’ or ‘how one knows right from wrong.’ In some instances συνείδησις may be equivalent to some organ of the body, for example, heart or liver, but generally some descriptive phrase proves to be the most satisfactory equivalent.

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to be seared in the conscience, or: to be seared as to one’s conscience) to be unwilling to learn from one’s conscience
s.g: to refuse to listen to one’s conscience; to be completely insensitive to

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: the movement of two or more objects to the same location{N:001}
s.g: to gather together; to come together; to go together; to meet; to assemble
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be together with someone
s.g: to be with

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: to come/go into together with
s.g: to go in with; to enter with

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: one who is away from home on a journey with someone else
s.g: travelling companion

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: pertaining to being selected together with
s.g: one who is also chosen; what is chosen together with
s.c: As indicated in some of the renderings of terms expressing choice and selection, it is often preferable, and frequently necessary, to indicate who does the choosing. Therefore, it is often advisable or necessary to indicate the agent, whether in an active or passive construction.

s.d: to be aware of information about something
s.g: to know; to be conscious of; to be aware of

s.d: to share information or knowledge with
s.g: to know something together with someone else
s.c: The sharing of information may be expressed in ⟦Acts 5:2|Acts 5:2⟧ as ‘his wife also knew about it.’

s.d: to acquire information, with focus upon the event of perception
s.g: to learn about; to find out about

s.d: to come to understand clearly on the basis of perceived information
s.g: to understand clearly; to realize fully; to become fully aware of
